# Sparse ancestors emit an included grandchild's delta twice

## Context

Ada's review of #19499 raised a finite-depth leapfrog hypothesis. A live unit-harness falsifier confirmed it: one sparse ancestor payload and its separately emitted grandchild both produce the same text delta. [Executed receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/8890#issuecomment-6082827380). This is extra work, not the lost update repaired by #8890; the final vnode is correct.

## The Problem

Initialize and settle root → parent → B, then:

```javascript
root.setSilent({style: {color: 'green'}, updateDepth: 2});
b.setSilent({text: 'B new'});
await root.promiseUpdate();
```

At `8f497d9f4e`, root's merged IDs contain B and its bridge parent. The batch emits root and B, and returns two identical `{id: B.id, textContent: 'B new'}` deltas. No fabricated merge entries are needed.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `VdomLifecycle.executeVdomUpdate` publishes a **disjoint** batch and says to remove child roots already covered by a parent. `VDomUpdate.getMergedChildIds` explicitly includes bridge ancestors. `TreeBuilder.#buildTree` expands allowlisted descendants even at the nominal depth boundary. The retained depth-only half of the collision predicate does not describe that actual sparse coverage.

The historical intent is recorded in #8834's [double-update investigation](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/8834#issuecomment-3774716327) and [later sparse-tree restoration](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/8834#issuecomment-3775227679). This leaf preserves both; it does not force every payload to depth 1.

## The Fix

Refine collision filtering in `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:executeVdomUpdate` so an actual sparse scope deduplicates by its retained allowlist, including a descendant at or beyond nominal depth. Dense scopes retain their depth coverage rule. Reuse the existing scope snapshot from #19499. A leapfrogged root whose payload is absorbed must retain its in-flight protection and callback ownership until adoption; the ancestor's nominal depth does not protect it. A predicate-only repair was falsified by the busy-Main browser control: a later promise observed the earlier vnode.

Extend the existing `SparseUpdates.spec.mjs` with the natural grandchild sequence and a dense-depth boundary control. No new module or public API is needed.

Decision Record impact: none; restoration of internal batch coverage. Contract Ledger: not applicable, no added or changed public/consumed signature.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A naturally merged grandchild at distance 2 under a sparse depth-2 ancestor produces exactly one new-text delta and adopts its new vnode.
- [ ] AC-2 A deeper bridge path is preserved, while clean sibling branches remain pruned.
- [ ] AC-3 A finite dense parent that does not reach the grandchild keeps that grandchild's separate root; depth-1 disjoint and full-depth controls still pass.
- [ ] AC-4 The excluded-sibling lost-update regression from #8890 remains fixed; related VDOM tests pass without adding a full-tree traversal or allowlist copy.
- [ ] AC-5 Browser E2E coverage exercises the real App → VDom → Main → App pipeline with dedicated and shared workers: the old duplicate-delta case fails before repair and passes afterward; assert Main's delta stream, real DOM, and adopted vnode. Include a second write after payload collection while Main is busy: its promise must settle only after the newer vnode is adopted. Unit tests alone do not satisfy this gate (operator direction, 2026-10-09).

## Out of Scope

No force-dense fallback, TreeBuilder protocol change, cross-window lifecycle redesign, claim of duplicated DOM content, or alteration of #19499's approved head.

## Avoided Traps

Deduplicating equal deltas after Helper runs would hide redundant payload construction and processing. Fix ownership before dispatch instead. Nominal depth cannot stand in for actual sparse inclusion.

## Ownership and sequencing

Sophie owns this bounded follow-up. Prerequisite #8890 / #19499 merged as `a43fdd381b` on 2026-10-09; implementation is now based on that accepted scope snapshot.
